name: vmware-aiops (agent skill)

hlido_opinion.headline: An installable agent skill for VMware AIOps distributed through skills.sh, with a real but modest adoption signal (a few hundred installs) — and a public surface too thin to judge what the skill actually does in depth.
hlido_opinion.body: vmware-aiops is a single agent skill published on the skills.sh directory, installable into coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others) with one command (`npx skills add vmware-skills/vmware-aiops`). Its one genuinely useful, verifiable signal is adoption: the listing reports a couple of hundred installs, which for a niche VMware operations skill is a real, if small, marker that people are actually pulling it. Beyond that, the reviewed public surface is the skills.sh directory chrome — navigation, topic lists, the install command and the install count — rather than a documentation page describing what the skill instructs an agent to do, what VMware operations it covers, or how it behaves. That is why this review is explicitly low-confidence and scored in the FADING band: not because the skill is poor, but because the captured evidence does not support a stronger claim. A skill is easy to install and inspect on GitHub, so the honest recommendation is to read its SKILL.md before relying on it. If a fuller surface (a dedicated skill page or repo README) is captured on re-test, this score should be revisited — the adoption signal suggests it may deserve better than a thin directory listing allows us to say today.

tier_rationale: FADING (56), low confidence — the one solid signal is a real if modest install count for a niche VMware AIOps skill, and it is a genuinely installable agent skill. It is not scored higher because the captured public surface is the skills.sh directory listing, not documentation of what the skill does, so there is no evidence base to credit depth or reliability. This is an evidence ceiling, not a judgement that the skill is weak; a fuller re-test could raise it.
what_it_does_well: A genuinely installable agent skill — one command (`npx skills add vmware-skills/vmware-aiops`) into common coding agents
A real, if modest, adoption signal (a few hundred installs) for a niche VMware operations use case
Open source and inspectable on GitHub, so its actual instructions can be read before use
what_it_fails_at: Reviewed surface is the skills.sh directory listing, not documentation of what the skill actually does
No captured detail on covered VMware operations, prerequisites, safety, or behaviour
No independent quality signal beyond an install counter
Single-skill, niche scope; maintenance cadence not visible on the captured surface
best_for: VMware operators already using an MCP/skills-capable coding agent who want an off-the-shelf AIOps skill to trial
Users comfortable reading a skill's SKILL.md on GitHub before relying on it
not_recommended_for: Anyone needing documented, supported, production-grade VMware automation with guarantees
Users who want a full product rather than a single installable agent skill
red_flags: Thin public surface: the captured page documents the skill's existence and install count but not its actual behaviour — inspect the SKILL.md before use.

compared_to.verdict_diff: devops-incident-response is a broader incident-response agent capability; vmware-aiops is a single, narrowly-scoped installable skill for VMware operations. Broader agent for general incident handling, vmware-aiops for a specific VMware AIOps task if its SKILL.md fits.

infrabroker brokers infrastructure operations more generally; vmware-aiops is a packaged skill on skills.sh scoped to VMware AIOps. Pick infrabroker for breadth, vmware-aiops for a drop-in VMware-specific skill.
